Yes. 

The story is written as a dramatic dialogue, which naturally aligns "story time" with "real-world time" (reading time). This real-time pacing is effectively balanced with the *compression* of the characters' backstory—nearly three years of estrangement, a shared history with a woman named Sabine, and unspoken grievances are condensed into a few brief, subtext-heavy exchanges. At the same time, the author slightly *stretches* pivotal moments in the present using stage directions that enforce silence and slow down the rhythm (e.g., *"Pause"*, *"nach einer Weile"*, *"Stille"*, and the moment they both stare at the fallen photo without picking it up). This manipulation of pacing creates palpable tension and makes Jonas's final decision to take off his jacket and stay feel earned and impactful.
